deleteBranch.localWarning: This deletes only the local branch, not the branch on the server. Git checks whether the branch is merged.
deleteBranch.localUnmergedWarning: This branch is not fully merged. Deleting it discards its unmerged commits.
deleteBranch.remoteWarning: This deletes the branch at the push destination shown below and affects other users. If fetch and push destinations differ, the local remote-tracking entry may remain.
deleteBranch.missingRemote: Cannot delete a remote branch without a known remote.
deleteBranch.unexpectedRemote: Local branch has an unexpected remote.
deleteBranch.invalidSnapshot: Could not prepare a complete branch deletion snapshot.
deleteBranch.destinationId: For network URLs, the SHA-256 identifier distinguishes the push destination without displaying credentials or paths.

fileSelection.discardTitle: Discard the changes of the selected files

dialog.title: Push branch
dialog.noRemotes: No remotes configured. Add one using Manage Remotes before pushing.
dialog.pushTagsHint: Turn this off when the remote rejects tag creation.

pull.title: Reconcile divergent branches
pull.description: Your branch “{{branch}}” and its remote both have new commits. Choose how to combine them.
pull.mergeExplanation: Keep your existing commits and create a merge commit joining both histories.
pull.rebaseExplanation: Replay your local commits on top of the remote branch. This rewrites local commits and changes their IDs. Avoid rebasing commits you have already shared.
pull.once: This choice applies only to this pull. Your Git settings will not change. Cancel leaves your commits untouched.
pull.conflict: Pull stopped. Resolve conflicts in Changes, then continue or abort.
